text:
maria: Heads-up — we've been seeing a lot of GPU node churn in eu-west during nightly batch jobs. median node lifetime dropped to ~18m last 3 nights, lots of scale-down followed by immediate scale-up.

jonathan: Yikes. Is CA aggressively evicting because of low pod density on GPUs?

maria: Looks like it. Current CA flags on the cluster: ```--expander=most-pods --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m --scale-down-unready-time=20m --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 --max-empty-bulk-delete=10```

kai: most-pods tends to favour node counts that maximize pod count, which can fragment GPUs. For GPU workloads we usually prefer least-waste or a weighted expander.

leah: Fragmentation + preemptible spot churn = repeated provision of new GPU nodes. Cost and cold-cache latency spikes.

devin: Can we try a short experiment: increase unneeded-time and lower utilization threshold so CA cools its heels, and flip expander to least-waste? I worry about tail latency for interactive workloads though.

maria: Proposed canary changes for eu-west-autoscaler (15m window experiment): ```--expander=least-waste --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m --scale-down-unready-time=25m --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.4 --max-empty-bulk-delete=3 --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false```

jonathan: max-empty-bulk-delete=3 is important — bulk deletes were nuking several under-provisioned nodegroups at once. Lowering it should reduce simultaneous evictions. :+1:

kai: Also recommend enabling --balance-similar-node-groups=false for the canary. Balancing tries to spread pods which is the opposite of GPU consolidation.

leah: What about pod priorities? We have some low-priority batch jobs labelled gpu:batch. If CA can't pack them, it still should avoid evicting higher-priority interactive pods.

maria: Plan: roll config to eu-west canary cluster now, let it run 48h across two night cycles, compare metrics: median node lifetime, number of scale-ups per hour, cost per GPU-hour, and 95p p99 tail latency for inference.

devin: Can you paste the kubectl patch you'll use?

maria: Patch (daemonset) for CA configmap rollout: ```kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap cluster-autoscaler-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"flags":"--expander=least-waste --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m --scale-down-unready-time=25m --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.4 --max-empty-bulk-delete=3 --balance-similar-node-groups=false"}}'```

sre-bot: deploy-bot: starting rollout of cluster-autoscaler (canary) to eu-west. Track with /rollouts/2798765432.

jonathan: Add a metric to alert if scale-up rate > 6/hour for more than 30m. That will catch misconfigurations that keep provisioning.

maria: Good call — I'll add a temporary grafana panel and PagerDuty rule for the canary.

kai: Also keep an eye on unschedulable pods and pending GPU requests. If we artificially prevent scale-down too long it could cause wasted capacity during prolonged idle periods. 15m is a conservative middle ground.

leah: How will this change affect Dedicated clusters vs Preemptible spots?

maria: This canary only for spot-backed nodegroups in eu-west. For dedicated pools we want faster reclaim but lower fragmentation — we'll run a separate test later with different thresholds (e.g., 8m unneeded, util 0.55).

devin: After 48h, if node churn drops and p95 tail latency is stable, we can standardize these flags for all spot GPU pools. If not, revert quickly.

jonathan: Can we also test expander=price+least-waste combo on another canary? price tends to pick cheaper instance types but can increase fragmentation. Might be worth a second axis.

maria: Yep — scheduling a follow-up canary with expander=price, same windows, on a small subset of nodegroups.

leah: Action items: maria - deploy canary + pagerduty alert; jonathan - add scale-up-rate alert; kai - prepare simulation to estimate packing improvement from least-waste vs most-pods; devin - prepare rollback playbook.

maria: Doing it now. I'll post results and raw metrics export after 48h.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed to eu-west (3 CA replicas).

jonathan: Thanks — we'll watch the dashboards. If the churn doesn't improve within one cycle, let's roll back and try increasing node affinity / bin-packing at the scheduler level instead.

maria: Noted — thanks everyone.
